issue_context.title: Add support for wikis to `gh repo view`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

A repo's wiki can be cloned if you attach `.wiki` to a repo's name. (i.e., `gh repo clone neovim/neovim.wiki`). However, if you run `gh repo view` for a repo's wiki, you will get an error.

For example, using the [neovim/neovim wiki](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki), the following error is received:

```console
$ gh repo view neovim/neovim.wiki
GraphQL: Could not resolve to a Repository with the name 'neovim/neovim.wiki'. (repository)

$ gh repo view neovim/neovim.wiki --web
GraphQL: Could not resolve to a Repository with the name 'neovim/neovim.wiki'. (repository)
```

### Proposed solution

I personally heavily use `gh repo view --web` to quickly navigate to the GitHub website. I would like the same experience when working on a repo's wiki locally. For example, this could send the user to the repo's wiki homepage (i.e., `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/wiki`). 

### Additional context

- This error was received on `v2.32.0`
    ```console
    $ gh --version
    gh version 2.32.0 (2023-07-11)
    https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.32.0
    ````
- Repository names ending in `.wiki` are reserved by GitHub
- Any repo's wiki can be clone by adding `.wiki` to the end of the repo name. (e.g., `gh repo clone neovim/neovim.wiki`, `git@github.com:neovim/neovim.wiki.git`, `https://github.com/neovim/neovim.wiki.git`)
comments:
> I personally heavily use `gh repo view --web` to quickly navigate to the GitHub website

```sh
for i in $manpath ;do find $i -name 'gh*' | xargs grep -l 'wiki' ;done
# /usr/local/share/man/man1/gh-repo-edit.1
# /usr/local/share/man/man1/gh-repo-create.1
# /usr/local/share/man/man1/gh-browse.1
```

- `gh browse` has a `--wiki` flag 

```sh
man gh-browse 
#       -w, --wiki
#             Open repository wiki
```

> * `gh browse` has a `--wiki` flag

When running `gh browse --wiki` in a local clone of a project's wiki, it does not resolve to the correct URL. It ends up going to `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}.wiki/wiki`. It is not the exact behaviour I would like, but it is close.

```console
$ gh browse
Opening github.com/neovim/neovim.wiki in your browser.

$ gh browse --wiki
Opening github.com/neovim/neovim.wiki/wiki in your browser.
```

Indeed, you have a valid point. 
This issue is similar to a previous case where `gh repo clone cli/cli.wiki` was reported as a [bug](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2477#issuecomment-733618820) (25/Nov/20) and later on fixed. Given this precedent, it's reasonable to suggest that this current issue could also be addressed. Alternatively, users could be guided to utilize the `--repo` flag.

```sh
gh browse --wiki --repo neovim/neovim
```

@arkinmodi Thanks for the report and @LangLangBart for the investigation. I reclassified this as a bug as using the `browse` command from a cloned wiki repository should work and bring the user to a valid URL. Going to open this up for contributions.
Raised[ PR ](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/7748) to fix this. Not sure how I could test this since bin/gh won't work inside a cloned local repo wiki.
Thanks @samcoe. Just to clarify would `gh repo view`/`gh repo view --web` also be a bug that needs to be fixed or just `gh browse` or just `gh browse --wiki`?

> @arkinmodi Thanks for asking, my previous comment was not fully clear on that. What would you expect the behavior to be for `repo view` and `repo view --web`?
> 
> In my opinion, I don't think displaying the wiki in the terminal is very useful as they are meant to be traversed through links which is not possible on the command line. For example displaying the `neovim/neovim` wiki would result in a large list of links that the user can't take any actions on. I think `repo view` should more or less ignore that it is being run from inside a wiki repository and instead display the repo that the wiki is attached to, and the same behavior when the `--web` flag is used.
> 
> For `browse`, I would also assume that without the `--wiki` flag that the user is brought to the repo that the wiki is attached.

Thanks for clarifying. I agree that essentially `OWNER/REPO.wiki` should just be an alias to `OWNER/REPO`. One case I was thinking about is that someone uses `gh browse` to open a file that is in the wiki repo, but I think it is best to let it just go to the 404 page.
